userRequest:
You are an agent version tracker. Check for new releases of the ORIGINAL upstream agent CLI products — NOT our babysitter plugin packages.

STEP 1: Build atlas.
```
npm run build --workspace=@a5c-ai/atlas
```

STEP 2: Get the target list using the SAME logic as `scripts/sync-external-plugin-repos.mjs` uses in `buildTargetsFromCatalog()`. Read that file to understand the pattern, then run:
```
node -e "
  import(new URL('file://' + process.cwd() + '/packages/atlas/dist/catalog/sdk.js').href)
    .then(m => {
      const targets = m.listPluginTargetDescriptors()
        .filter(t => t.externalRepo)
        .map(t => ({
          id: t.adapterName || t.targetId,
          displayName: t.displayName,
          cliCommand: t.cliCommand,
          externalPackageName: t.externalPackageName,
          externalRepo: t.externalRepo,
        }));
      console.log(JSON.stringify(targets, null, 2));
    });
"
```
This gives you every agent that has an external repo — these are the upstream host agents. The `externalPackageName` is the npm package to check (if set). For agents without an npm package, search the web.

Also check adapter source for additional install commands:
```
grep -r 'npm install -g' packages/adapters/codecs/src/ | grep -v node_modules | grep -v test
```
Merge both lists. EXCLUDE all @a5c-ai/* packages.

STEP 3: For EACH upstream agent, check the latest published version. `npm view <package>@latest version` for npm packages. Search the web for agents distributed differently (pip, binary, etc.).

STEP 4: Compare against AgentVersion records in the graph. Read files in `packages/atlas/graph/agent-stack/agent-versions/` and `packages/atlas/graph/agent-stack/products/` to see what versions are already recorded.

STEP 5: For new versions not in the graph:
- Search the web for release notes, changelog, blog posts
- Create or update the AgentVersion YAML
- Note capability changes, new CLI flags, breaking changes, transport/API changes

STEP 6: If graph files changed:
- Rebuild: `npm run build --workspace=@a5c-ai/atlas`
- Branch: `agent-versions/daily-$(date +%Y-%m-%d)`
- Commit all changes, create ONE PR against staging

STEP 7: For each new agent+version pair, check for existing issue: `gh issue list --label "agent-version-update" --search "<agent> <version>"`

If none exists, create an issue. The issue body must NOT be a static template — fill it with the ACTUAL research you did. Include exact version numbers, links to release notes/changelog/blog post, real change summary, affected system surfaces, install/package changes, migrations, and a specific assimilation checklist. Use labels `agent-version-update,graph-update`.

STEP 8: Print a summary table with ALL agents checked.

IMPORTANT: Cover every upstream agent systematically. Do not stop after one. One PR for all changes in this run.
